newsitem.title: USA: Indian tax cuts will boost investment-Chidambaram.
newsitem.headline: Indian tax cuts will boost investment-Chidambaram.

text.p: Indian Finance Minister P. Chidambaram said across-the-board tax cuts in the country's budget for the coming financial year would foster economic growth through an expected rise in savings and investment.

In a speech from India via live video feed to the second annual Wharton India Economic Forum on Friday, Chidambaran said tax cuts would stimulate the economy and bring in more revenue for the government.
"The household and the public sectors should be encouraged to save more," he said, noting that higher savings would lead to more investment and stronger economic growth.

The budget for the fiscal year ending March 31, 1998, announced on February 28, slashed income tax rates by 10 percent, reduced corporate taxes and other tariffs and raised the ceiling for foreign institutional investments on Indian firms.
To curb inflation, Chidambaram affirmed the government's commitment to keeping a tight rein on credit.
The M-3 money supply is projected to grow at 16 percent and the inflation rate to remain at 6.0 percent in the 1997/1998 fiscal year, he said.

Without dwelling on the anticipated rise in social spending in the budget, he forecast that the ratio of the fiscal deficit to gross domestic product (GDP) would fall to 4.5 percent by the end of the next fiscal year from the current 5.0 percent.
GDP growth should remain at seven percent for the next two to three years, he added.

The market-friendly budget was expected to attract strong foreign investment flows into India, especially for infrastructure projects in oil exploration, telecommunications and the power sector, Chidambaram said.
Privatisation of core state-owned enterprises would also bring in revenue, he said.

Chidambaram admitted the government was concerned about recent volatility in Indian stock markets, which has kept small investors away. Bombay's stock market index initially surged on optimism over the new budget but has since lost most of those gains.
